Hi Evan — appreciate the note and the profile. Forwarding a short recommendation and the package matrix for clarity.

Short answer up front: for a 3-month pilot that needs p95 <= 350ms on chat generation, we usually recommend the Compact-Throughput starter with a small dedicated buffer (burst pool) and prefix caching enabled. It keeps token cost lower while the burst handles spikes.

What I’m attaching: MedCore_Package_Matrix_v3.xlsx — includes:
- Starter config (Compact-Throughput) with estimated monthly tokens and cost
- Upgrade path to Throughput-Plus (predictable commit) including prorated credits and how they apply
- A sample canary rollout plan so you can swap model variants without downtime

Mechanics / highlights:
- Mid-contract upgrades: we pro-rate remaining committed months and apply a credit toward the new monthly commit. No penalty to move up.
- Downgrades: allowed at next renewal window; we recommend a 30-day notice to avoid immediate disruption.
- Discounts: standard renewal concessions range from 7-12% for 12-month commitments; larger TCVs get case-by-case pricing (Ben is copied for escalation).

Next steps:
1) If you want, we can schedule a 30-min packaging workshop (I’ll bring Ben to run numbers).
2) Share an expected TCV range so we can model renewal concessions.

Thanks — I’ll ping Ben to run through discount buckets for you.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Kim / Lauren — forwarding Evan’s ask and Kim’s recommendation. Quick internal notes (please keep to thread):

- If MedCore signals 3x throughput growth on month 2, I’d put them into a mid-tier commit (Throughput-Plus) with a 6-month ramp. That keeps latency SLOs and gives us predictable GPU allocation.
- Concession guidance: for a 12-month commit in the $250k-$500k TCV range we can standardly offer 9% discount + one-time onboarding credits (equivalent to 1 month of Compact-Throughput). If they go >$500k, we move to 12% + dedicated onboarding assistance.
- Pricing note: include optional quantization/throughput tuning as a billable professional service or roll into the onboarding credit.

Questions:
1) Kimberly — do we want to offer a short-term trial discount for the initial pilot to lower friction (e.g., 20% off first month limited to token charges)?
2) Lauren — any constraints from finance on offering a DocuSign amendment with a short-term credit clause?

Ben
